stories.title: Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia raises critical questions about the future of AI
stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been a singular figure in the development of the AI industry, which suddenly has to survive without him.

sources.title: Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia raises critical questions about the future of AI
sources.text: Michael Dell described Jensen Huang as a "visionary of the AI age." Deutsche Telekom CEO Tim Höttges said a photo with the Nvidia CEO produced more media coverage for his company than its iPhone launch. During the keynote of his annual Dreamforce conference, Salesforce's Marc Benioff said, "Jensen, we're all following you, bro," as the two paced through the audience. Follow CNBC's live coverage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation His fame extended way beyond tech. In May, Huang joined President Donald Trump on Air Force One for a trip to China to meet with President Xi Jinping . Three months later, Huang gathered six of the biggest names at the Nasdaq to announce on CNBC a proposed $500 billion artificial intelligence buildout plan, cementing his central role at the intersection of Wall Street and Silicon Valley. As Nvidia became the first company to rip past a $5 trillion market cap, bending the laws of physics with its advanced graphics processing units and pushing the AI boom to seemingly endless bounds, the now 63-year-old Huang, clad in a black leather jacket, traversed the globe as the face of the brand powering the next industrial revolution. Over the past week it all came crashing down. Following two reported extramarital affairs — one with an alleged Chinese spy and another with an employee — Huang is leaving the company he co-founded 33 years ago in crisis, and thrusting the AI market into chaos. The board is now left to pick a successor for a company that's been run by a singular figure with no second-in-command. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. Harvey Jones has been appointed chairman. Nvidia has not responded to multiple requests for comment. "How companies handle a crisis determines their future," former Cisco CEO John Chambers, now a startup investor, told CNBC's " Fast Money " on Wednesday. "How they handle this will determine if they're a great company and a great leadership team beyond one person." It had been a tumultuous stretch for Nvidia, even before the Huang saga led the board to launch an investigation of the CEO's behavior and the potential national security implications. The stock is on pace for its sixth straight weekly drop, which would be the longest losing streak since 2012. That includes a 9% slump last week after the midterm elections resulted in sweeping Democratic victories in both chambers of Congress, and the passage of dozens of ballot measures that could slow the buildout of new data centers. Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly results on Tuesday, and expectations remain high, with analysts projecting 92% year-over-year revenue growth to $109.2 billion, according to LSEG. That's up 18-fold from the same quarter in 2022, just before OpenAI launched ChatGPT and kicked off the generative AI era. It's a historic level of growth for any business, and particularly notable for a company that spent most of its first few decades as a niche technology provider for video games. Huang founded Nvidia to make chips for computer graphics, both for video games and rendering. In the early 2000s, he and other executives saw an opportunity to put GPUs to work for computationally intense projects. That technology eventually turned Nvidia into the most important player in AI and a key American asset for national defense. In the process, Huang became the ultimate decider, choosing how, when and where GPUs get allocated. The biggest buyers were the hyperscalers — Amazon, Google , Meta and Microsoft — which needed the chips to build their own AI services and make them available to cloud customers. OpenAI , meanwhile, was snapping up GPUs for its powerful models and consumer apps. To expand his customer base, Huang designated compute capacity to a number of so-called neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius , putting equity into the companies and helping them build big businesses around renting out GPUs. Oracle gobbled up billions of dollars worth of GPUs, going heavily into debt in the process. Elon Musk's xAI, now part of SpaceX , did the same to build its Grok model, before eventually starting to rent out excess capacity to Anthropic and Google. Huang wanted the world standardizing on Nvidia. Last year he demanded that Oracle buy additional Nvidia networking hardware if it wanted allocation to its state-of-the-art Grace Blackwell chips, said two people familiar with the deal who asked not to be named because the negotiations were private. In August, Nvidia said it will provide up to $105 billion in financing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio that could be the largest of its kind in the world. "He created the product that started the industry," said Chris Miglino, CEO of neocloud Axe Compute . " Without his leadership we may be many years behind where we are today with AI chip technology, which is the driving force behind the neocloud market." When it comes to investing cash in fledgling startups, Huang is known to host entrepreneurs at Nvidia's Silicon Valley headquarters. While there could be 30 Nvidia employees in the room for the pitch meeting, only Huang asks questions, according to people with knowledge of the matter, who requested anonymity because they're not authorized to speak publicly about it. One source told CNBC that key aspects of project finance are so reliant on Huang's sign-off that, when he travels, those involved in the deal are forced to wait for his plane to land before learning if they can go forward or if terms have to be renegotiated. Huang's ambitions extended well beyond the U.S. He wanted to be a force in China, which became a difficult market for Nvidia during the Biden administration and was virtually off-limits after Trump implemented strict export controls in his second term. Huang's aggressive pursuit of China may have been his undoing. sources.title: Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO just got harder after Jensen Huang’s dramatic exit as Nvidia CEO
sources.text: Anthropic is about to embark on one of the most hotly anticipated IPOs in history. After a dramatic turn of events, it will now be doing so a week after the industry lost one of its most powerful figures and best salesmen. Nvidia’s longtime CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang resigned from the company on Thursday following reports alleging he had engaged in two extramarital affairs: one with a customer suspected by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese intelligence asset and another with an Nvidia executive who reports to him. The timing has thrown new pressure on Anthropic’s listing, which was already seen as a stress test for investors’ appetite for AI. The AI lab is expected to list on Wednesday or Thursday next week, days after Nvidia reports quarterly earnings—the company’s first-ever without Huang at the helm. Nvidia is a close partner of Anthropic and intimately involved in the lab’s upcoming IPO. According to Anthropic’s filings, the chipmaker has agreed to buy about $10 billion of shares in a $26 billion private placement alongside the IPO. The two companies are also closely tied commercially, with Anthropic committing to tens of billions of dollars to secure access to Nvidia’s most advanced chips. Investors and analysts told Fortune that while they don’t expect the Nvidia shock to affect Anthropic’s core business, it could cause problems for the broader AI story. Jay Goldberg, an analyst at Seaport Research Partners and one of the few on Wall Street with a sell rating on Nvidia’s stock, doesn’t expect Huang’s exit to derail the deal. “They’re going to go public right in the face of Nvidia’s earnings call, and I don’t think that derails it,” he said. “It’s such a massive IPO and there’s so many people behind it now that they don’t pull the IPO.” The bigger risk, he said, comes once Anthropic is a public company. Speaking shortly before Huang’s departure but after reports that he was likely to be leaving the company, Goldberg warned that turmoil at Nvidia, including the loss of its CEO, would create a headwind for Anthropic when it reports its first quarterly results. “At the very least it will create this narrative of, ‘Can the AI narrative maintain? Can we keep doing this?’” he said. “They’ll get much tougher questions.” Karl Alomar, a partner at venture firm M13, agreed that Anthropic’s fundamentals haven’t changed. “From where I stand, Anthropic is still in as good, as strong a position as it was before this news came out,” he said. “Anthropic’s numbers are fantastic, and they’ve clearly shown that they have excess capacity for what they need. They haven’t spent that much money.” Anthropic is also less dependent on Nvidia than some of its rivals, running some models on Google’s TPUs, Amazon’s Trainium chips, and AMD’s GPUs, as well as Nvidia’s hardware. Anthropic has also reportedly been exploring building its own chips. “Nvidia has committed to invest $10 billion in the Anthropic IPO. That will likely still happen when the IPO eventually happens,” said Francine McKenna, an accountant and investigative journalist who has taught at the Wharton School. “But anyone who was looking at Nvidia to bail out CoreWeave if needed should probably look elsewhere.” However, the recent trouble at Nvidia and questions surrounding the CEO’s judgement could spill over into more scrutiny for its partners, according to Jason Schloetzer, an associate professor at Georgetown University’s McDonough School of Business. He said he expected there to be “much closer scrutiny of [Anthropic’s] ties to Nvidia and customers associated with Nvidia.” For Silicon Valley, Anthropic and competitor OpenAI have needed so much capital that almost every venture capital firm in town owns a piece of them—making them the private market equivalent of an index fund. That makes Anthropic’s expected IPO next week a high-stakes liquidity event—not only for the more than 400 backers of Anthropic, but for the AI boom as a whole. There’s a broad sense that if Anthropic succeeds, the AI boom has far more runway. If it flops or pushes back indefinitely, it would be an unequivocal negative signal that the AI bubble is heading towards a pop. It may not be a bust. Indeed, at least one venture capitalist sees a clear upside for Anthropic. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has long pushed for tighter controls on chip exports to China, putting him at odds with Huang. The AI lab has similarly clashed with Huang on AI regulation, with Huang particularly keen to avoid any licensing requirements that would make it more difficult for customers to adopt open-source AI models. “If anything, I think Anthropic is a beneficiary here,” said the investor, who asked not to be named given the situation’s sensitivity and their investments across AI. “They weren’t that close to Jensen…They’re building their own chip, and so the supply chain considerations that get freed up are good for Anthropic.”

sources.title: Jensen Huang renuncia ao cargo de CEO da Nvidia após admitir traição
sources.text: Por Gabriel Cavalheiro | 12/11/2026 às 11:48 • Atualizado 12/11/2026 às 11:56 O CEO e cofundador da Nvidia, Jensen Huang, renunciou ao cargo nesta quinta-feira (12) , após admitir publicamente uma relação extraconjugal com a ex-diretora da Megaspeed International e empresária Alice Huang. A executiva é investigada por espionagem a serviço do Ministério de Segurança do Estado da China. A atual CFO da empresa, Colette Kress, foi nomeada CEO interina enquanto o conselho busca por um novo executivo para assumir o cargo. A renúncia de Huang acontece após 33 anos na liderança da Nvidia, que tem vivido um dos seus melhores momentos por liderar o boom da inteligência artificial e fornecer componentes para data centers de IA. No ano passado, a empresa foi a primeira do mundo a ultrapassar os valores de mercado de US$ 4 trilhões e US$ 5 trilhões. A relação extraconjugal entre o ex-CEO da Nvidia e Alice Huang levantou preocupações sobre a segurança nacional dos Estados Unidos e o mercado de chips de IA . No último domingo (8), o ex-chefão da companhia de chips admitiu a traição em meio a um escândalo de espionagem chinesa . "Fui infiel à minha esposa. Minhas ações a machucaram, assim como aos nossos filhos. Não há desculpa para o que fiz. Sinto muito", escreveu o então CEO. O jornal The New York Times relatou que Jensen Huang estaria envolvido em um segundo caso , desta vez com a vice-presidente de health care da Nvidia e subordinada direta do ex-CEO, Kimberly Powell , segundo cinco funcionários da companhia. As políticas internas da Nvidia orientam os funcionários a “evitar situações em que nossas ações criem conflito”, incluindo “relacionamentos pessoais”. O acúmulo de escândalos envolvendo o ex-presidente fez com que as ações da empresa caíssem 8% nesta quarta-feira (11). A companhia também perdeu US$ 1 trilhão de valor de mercado . Em comunicado enviado à imprensa, o conselho da Nvidia agradeceu as contribuições de Jensen. "A Nvidia é uma das empresas de tecnologia mais impactantes do mundo. O conselho e a empresa agradecem a Jensen por suas contribuições imensuráveis para a companhia e para a indústria", diz a mensagem. A companhia está iniciando uma busca por um Chief Executive Officer permanente e considerará candidatos internos e externos . Até lá, Kress ocupará o cargo de CEO de forma interina. “A força da Nvidia sempre veio de suas pessoas e, junto com nossa equipe de liderança, estou comprometida em construir sobre a base extraordinária que Jensen criou ao longo dos últimos 33 anos”, destacou a executiva. O empresa também anunciou que Harvey C. Jones assumirá a posição de primeiro presidente do conselho. Na próxima terça-feira (17), a Nvidia divulgará seus resultados financeiros referentes ao terceiro trimestre do ano fiscal de 2027. Vale lembrar que, em setembro, a companhia adquiriu a Hugging Face, o que levantou a dúvida se a plataforma continuará com código aberto após a compra.

sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following affairs scandal
sources.text: Nvidia Corp.’s board of directors today announced the resignation of Jensen Huang, now former chief executive and president of the artificial intelligence chipmaker, amid a scandal, naming Colette Kress, current executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO. The news arrives following numerous industry reports that the board intended to replace Huang as CEO after revelations of a second extramarital relationship with an executive at Nvidia, coming mere days after he admitted to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. News initially broke over the weekend that Huang had an affair with Alice Huang , no relation, an executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd. and an alleged Chinese spy. The Information reported on Tuesday that Alice Huang facilitated $7.5 billion in chip sales to China. According to another report, Jensen Huang also had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, who serves as vice president of healthcare. The New York Times reported last month that U.S. authorities concluded Alice Huang acted as a Chinese intelligence asset. Upon revelations of the affair, the Associated Press reported that President Trump announced that the Federal Bureau of Investigation was looking into the allegations, while adding, “I think that he’ll be in good shape.” Late Wednesday, the Nvidia board met to decide whether to oust Huang and discussed a potential replacement as CEO. Huang has no obvious single successor and owns about 3.6% of Nvidia’s stock. Reportedly, the board sought counsel from an outside firm to find someone to fill the role. With the announcement, Nvidia stock was falling more than 4% in early trading today, backing off an even steeper loss at the opening. Yahoo Finance calculated that Nvidia has lost more than $600 billion in market value since the previous Thursday, likely with more shocks to come. “Nvidia’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” said Kress. “We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead.” Kress has served as executive vice president and CFO since joining in September 2013. Her accolades include leading the company’s finance organization and working to build the company’s dominance in the AI chip industry. Before joining Nvidia, she spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco Systems Inc. and Microsoft Corp. The CFO was intimately involved with Nvidia’s widespread financing of AI compute providers, in particular its backing of not only AI leaders OpenAI Group PBC and Anthropic PBC — the latter set to go public as early as next week — but also neoclouds such as CoreWeave Inc. Those financings have been criticized by some as “circular,” meaning Nvidia essentially invested in customers so they could use the money to buy more of its graphics processing units. The potential successors to Huang, who had 30 direct reports, include no one obvious choice and a succession plan apparently was not in place. Candidates that some have speculated about include Arm Ltd. CEO Rene Haas, who worked at Nvidia years ago, Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, and Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president and general manager of hyperscale and high-performance computing and creator of its CUDA software considered its real moat for its business. “The sudden resignation of Jensen Huang is about more than succession at the world’s most important AI chipmaker,” Forrester Vice President and Group Research Director Stephanie Balaouras told SiliconANGLE in an email. “Nvidia’s leadership crisis is a stress test for the AI boom. If Nvidia stabilizes quickly under new leadership, the AI infrastructure boom will have demonstrated resilience. If its stock, financing relationships or ecosystem commitments remain under sustained pressure, that would add evidence to the fragile side of the AI bubble ledger.”” Balaouras added that “tech leaders shouldn’t overreact, but they should treat Nvidia’s CEO transition as a prompt to reassess concentration risk across their AI infrastructure, suppliers and investment plans.” Huang is best known for co-founding Nvidia in 1993 and has served as its CEO since. His departure will likely send further ripples through the AI silicon and software industry. He has been deeply involved in Nvidia’s product strategy and built longstanding customer relationships, helming the company as it became the colossal behemoth it is today. Nvidia commands roughly 80% of the data-center AI chip market, although industry estimates vary by methodology. Epoch Artificial Intelligence Inc. puts its share of AI computing power shipped at 63% in the second quarter of 2026. Other market carve-outs include custom chips built by cloud companies within the broader supply, including Google LLC’s tensor processing units at 25%, Amazon Inc.’s custom silicon at 5% and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s AI hardware accelerators at 4%. Nvidia is expected to report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings on Nov. 17. Support our mission to keep content open and free by engaging with theCUBE community. sources.text: After the leather-jacketed CEO, president, and co-founder of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, his company initially announced an investigation. However, The New York Times reported on Wednesday that there was evidence of another affair, this time with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him. A board meeting that night ended with Huang’s resignation , and Nvidia CFO Colette Kress was installed as the new interim CEO. Recent reporting noted that since last year, US intelligence reports had identified Alice Huang (no relation) as not only the exec for an AI compute company renting access to Nvidia GPUs, but also a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. The second report focused on Huang and Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, claiming that a bystander who recorded the two being “affectionate” at the hotel hosting Nvidia’s GTC developer conference in May was met by Huang’s security workers and asked to sign a non-disclosure agreement. In recent years, Nvidia has become a key part of the Trump administration’s AI push, a central figure in negotiations over potential Chinese access to cutting-edge AI hardware, and a company that has used its now $4 trillion-plus market cap to finance other AI companies, including the “neoclouds” like Coreweave who have been some of its biggest customers. Nvidia’s board announced that Jensen Huang — its longtime co-founder, president, and CEO — has resigned after reports of two extramarital affairs, one with an alleged Chinese spy and one with an Nvidia executive who reported to Huang. Following a late Wednesday night meeting, the board accepted Huang’s letter of resignation as CEO, president, and board member, effective immediately, with current CFO Colette Kress appointed interim CEO. Kress has been with Nvidia since 2013, with previous stops at Cisco and Microsoft. Nvidia is also changing its corporate structure in Huang’s absence, appointing former Synopsys CEO Harvey C. Jones as the first board chair in its history. The statement does not include a statement from Huang, while Kress is quoted as saying: Today, we’re talking about the Jensen Huang scandal at Nvidia, which is developing so quickly that we had to do an emergency update of this intro minutes before publishing this episode. Huang just resigned from his position as CEO of Nvidia as news of his affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy, threatened to engulf the company. Now that Nvidia’s CEO has resigned, the president posted on Truth Social calling for the former CEO of Apple to take over the company, for some reason. Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia this morning, a company he co-founded in 1993. The decision came following the company’s board opening an investigation into multiple extramarital affairs Huang had with a direct report and an alleged Chinese spy. The new, and first, Chair of the Board, Harvey Jones, shared news of Huang’s resignation with the company in an email, which also announced CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. You can read the full text of the board’s internal memo and Kress’s first message to employees as interim CEO below. Aside from his extramarital affairs , the Nvidia CEO also went viral this week over online images that show him wearing a vintage Saint Laurent jacket by Hedi Slimane — a studded switch up from his usual leather outerwear. Vanity Fair confirmed these are AI fakes that carry SynthID markers however, manipulated from photographs taken in June. Before a New York Times report claimed there’s evidence of a second affair by Jensen Huang and reports surfaced that Nvidia’s board could meet today to determine his fate, US Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez spoke to TMZ last night , focusing on asking why our economy depends on “five guys in tuxedos” being able to keep it in their pants. With reports that the company’s board is meeting to oust Huang from the company he co-founded , Bloomberg reports the board has been working with an unnamed outside firm to identify candidates and is considering naming a temporary chief executive while continuing to look for a permanent replacement. According to Semafor , the list includes Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, who was reportedly “ seriously considering ” leaving the company last year before deciding to stay , with some board members favoring Nvidia CFO Colette Kress instead. Nvidia’s board is preparing to dismiss CEO Jensen Huang following a report from The New York Times about a second alleged extramarital affair , just days after he admitted to a separate affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, The Wall Street Journal reports . The second alleged affair was with an executive who reports to him, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell, according to the Times . The Nvidia board will meet as soon as Wednesday night to decide on Huang’s future at the company, according to the Journal . Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment from The Verge . “When reached by phone Wednesday and asked about his relationship with Ms. Powell, Mr. Huang said, ‘I don’t think you should be talking to me directly.‘ He then hung up.” Great stuff, sir. This is the funniest way for the bubble to pop . Do stick around for the NDA anecdote in the kicker — sure seems like his security guards just have a stack of paperwork at the ready for his bullshit! Update: The WSJ reports Nvidia’s board is “preparing to oust” its CEO. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick about failing to put the alleged Chinese spy-run company on a list of national security concerns, Axios reports , though the Commerce Department denied the interaction. Meanwhile, The Wall Street Journal reports that Huang’s birthplace of Taiwan has been unnerved by his affair , where some view it as a national security threat, and it could play into upcoming local elections. sources.title: The Jensen Huang scandal is hardly over
sources.text: A second affair has hit the news cycle, but that’s not what matters here. A second affair has hit the news cycle, but that’s not what matters here. I was certain, until the story of Jensen Huang’s second affair hit, that Huang was bulletproof. After all, why wouldn’t he be? He’s placed himself indispensably at the center of the AI industry and famously had no succession plan at Nvidia. In fact, he’s the only CEO Nvidia has ever had. L’état c’est moi. Then two stories were published nearly back to back on Wednesday: one alleging Huang had an affair with his subordinate Kimberly Powell, another that the board was meeting to consider his ouster. First thing Thursday morning, Nvidia announced Huang had resigned. One of the most powerful men in Silicon Valley was out. Why throw Huang under the bus for getting his nuts drained? Fascinating. First of all, when I asked on Monday “Who else is Jensen Huang fucking?” I did not expect to get answers this fast — somebody, potentially somebody on the board (as we’ve seen in other incidents ), wanted the story out there. Second, why throw Huang under the bus for getting his nuts drained? This is not an industry that cares about that kind of thing — just ask Eric Schmidt and Bill Gates. My guess is that the second affair is a pretext for action, and this all goes back to the original story from last week: that Huang was honeypotted by an alleged Chinese spy. Whatever was going on with neocloud Megaspeed might be much, much worse than we know, and what we know is pretty bad : business listings that led to “a Malaysian data center and shopping mall, a near-empty office in Singapore and a dilapidated storefront outside Kuala Lumpur.” Even months before the report that Alice “No Relation” Huang, an exec at Megaspeed, was having an affair with Huang, there were questions about Nvidia’s business in China. The US government has placed strict export controls on Nvidia’s high-end chips. Huang claimed in May that as a result, Nvidia has zero percent market share in China . But also in May, short sellers Culper Research published a report in which they wrote, “We believe that in reality, over 20% of Nvidia’s FY 2026 compute revenues remained driven by China – supported both by illegal GPU diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries.” Megaspeed was Nvidia’s largest Southeast Asian buyer, but Singaporean newspaper The Straits Times visited Megaspeed’s Singapore office a month ago to find “no signs of activity.” Another building tenant told the reporters, “It is always dark for as long as it has been here. I hardly see anyone visiting or in the office.” The sole director of Megaspeed, Tan Yong Pong, appears to have vanished . The Singaporean company that owns Megaspeed, Swiftdata, has listed an office that belongs to an interior design firm as its business address. Incidentally, Alice Huang has surfaced in Beijing . The Financial Times says she’s barred from Singapore for giving police “inaccurate information.” Oh, and reportedly her companies invested in Chinese AI company DeepSeek and promised them Nvidia’s Blackwell chips? Fun! Megaspeed is only part of the story, I think. There are two Chinese chip-related scandals that could cause serious problems for Nvidia, and both feature people with close ties to Huang. One is Megaspeed, which involves Huang’s maybe-spy affair partner. The other centers on Super Micro (which, horribly, does business as Supermicro), a partner of Nvidia run by one of Huang’s old friends, Charles Liang. Super Micro’s cofounder, Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, along with Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang and Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun, allegedly defrauded the US by serving as a passthrough for a front company to buy $2.5 billion of Nvidia chips for Alibaba. The front company, not named in the indictment, is Thailand-based OBON , according to Bloomberg . Liang and Super Micro have not been charged. But these incidents may not be the end of Nvidia’s problems. Take for instance, more recently, New Matrix — another company that barely exists , and yet is an approved buyer of Nvidia chips. It is, in fact, one of several approved companies that “have ties to firms that have been blacklisted by the U.S. government, or that work as military contractors in China,” according to The New York Times. The question, of course, is how high this all goes Huang has insisted that Nvidia has seen “no evidence of any AI chip diversion.” He’s been pretty emphatic on that point , actually. I am now wondering if that is even a little bit true. If the board is cutting Huang loose, there’s probably more on chip smuggling allegations coming. More substantively, Nvidia reportedly intervened in a 2025 Commerce Department investigation of Megaspeed , which was suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips — halting the investigation. Since the scandal broke, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick appears to have become the fall guy for this, with Axios reporting that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent “confronted” him about failing to note Megaspeed as a national security concern and Politico saying “ more than half a dozen Republicans have demanded answers” from him . The question, of course, is how high this all goes. After all, Huang was awfully buddy-buddy with President Donald Trump, who was informed about Huang’s maybe-spy girlfriend in 2025 and apparently did nothing about it. Incidentally, Nvidia has reportedly donated $25 million to Trump’s planned ballroom . This is what gangster tech regulation looks like. I wonder what else was an open secret at the company, you know? Come January, Elizabeth Warren will be able to send subpoenas in her role as the chair of the Senate Banking Committee. And wouldn’t you know, she seems to be pretty interested . Democrats will control both the House and the Senate. Their voters have given them a mandate to root out corruption. And boy howdy, does Nvidia look like a sitting duck right now. sources.title: Ex-NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang is set to testify before Congress this month
sources.text: House Foreign Affairs Chair Brian Mast said the hearing will take place before Thanksgiving. Jensen Huang might have stepped down from his roles at the top of NVIDIA, but he won't be sliding out of the spotlight just yet. The company's former CEO and president is set to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, according to House representatives. House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast said Huang agreed to testify on Wednesday — hours before NVIDIA announced his resignation with immediate effect — after lawmakers threatened him with a subpoena. It appears the hearing will take place behind closed doors (which is unfortunate, because that's likely to be some spicy testimony). However, Mast expects it to be filmed and transcribed, according to Bloomberg . The House's Intelligence and China-focused committees will join the Foreign Affairs cohort for the hearing. "Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but NVIDIA is a very important company to the United States of America," Mast said. "I don't want to see anything hurt in NVIDIA, but he has some very serious questions to answer." NVIDIA has been in turmoil after it emerged over the weekend that the company was investigating Huang over an affair to which he admitted, allegedly with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. President Donald Trump said the FBI is investigating the situation as well. On Wednesday, it was reported that Huang had another affair, this time with Kimberly Powell, an NVIDIA executive who reported to him. The company's board met later that day to determine Huang's future. Colette Kress, NVIDIA's executive vice president and chief financial officer, is stepping in as interim CEO while the company seeks a permanent successor. Meanwhile, the Department of Justice is reportedly investigating Alice Huang , the alleged spy, to determine whether entities associated with her were involved in attempts to smuggle Super Micro Computer products to China. The DoJ is also said to be taking the lead in an investigation into her former company, the Singapore-based Megaspeed International, over alleged smuggling of US-made chips into China in defiance of export restrictions. The company said it would cooperate with the probe . Officials in Singapore opened an investigation into Alice Huang, Megaspeed and associated individuals last year. The Ministry of Home Affairs said in a statement on Thursday that she was barred from re-entering the country after police determined she knowingly offered up inaccurate information to downplay her role in Megaspeed. However, they "concluded that there was insufficient evidence to establish that Huang had committed any offences relating to the possible inaccurate declarations for which Megaspeed was being investigated." The investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals is ongoing.

sources.title: Trump pide a Tim Cook como CEO de NVIDIA tras la renuncia de Jensen Huang: «Una leyenda por otra leyenda»
sources.text: La renuncia de Jensen Huang como CEO de NVIDIA es, sin dudas, el tema del día . El escándalo por infidelidades le ha costado al empresario el puesto que ostentó durante los últimos 33 años , y el asunto promete seguir dando que hablar por bastante tiempo. Lo más curioso es que todos tienen una opinión sobre el tema y hasta Donald Trump ha propuesto a un reemplazante de alto perfil: Tim Cook . En las horas posteriores a la salida de Jensen Huang, Trump usó su perfil en Truth Social para postular a Cook como próximo CEO de NVIDIA. De acuerdo con el presidente de Estados Unidos, el exCEO de Apple es la única persona que tiene lo necesario para hacerse cargo de un rol tan complejo. A sabiendas de cómo piensa y actúa Donald Trump, no quedan dudas de que el mandatario estadounidense habla en serio. Claro que hoy parece improbable que Tim Cook esté dispuesto a asumir un rol tan notorio fuera de Apple, en especial por lo repentino y desastroso del desenlace de Jensen Huang. "Ahora que el CEO de NVIDIA, Jensen Huang, quien ha hecho un trabajo fantástico, ha renunciado, solo hay un hombre capaz de tomar su lugar: Tim Cook, de Apple. ¡Una leyenda reemplaza a otra leyenda! Presidente Donald J. Trump", publicó el presidente de Estados Unidos. Más allá de las virtudes de Jensen Huang y Tim Cook para conducir durante gran cantidad de años (y con gran éxito) a sus respectivas empresas, Trump no ofrece detalles de por qué el exjefe de Apple debería reemplazar a su antiguo colega en NVIDIA. Tal vez solo sea porque Cook ha sabido congraciarse con el presidente estadounidense durante sus mandatos, tal y como lo hizo Huang en su momento. Sea como sea, todavía no se sabe quién reemplazará definitivamente a Jensen Huang. Colette Kress , la jefa de finanzas de NVIDIA, fungirá de CEO interina hasta que se designe a un nuevo responsable del cargo. La junta del gigante verde anunció la puesta en marcha de un proceso de búsqueda de nuevo consejero delegado, para la cual analizará a candidatos internos y externos. Asimismo, se ha designado a Harvey C. Jones como presidente del board , el primero en ocupar ese rol en la historia de la compañía. ¿Tiene posibilidades Tim Cook de ser el próximo CEO de NVIDIA? Hasta hace menos de 15 días, era inaudito pensar en dicha empresa sin Jensen Huang como jefe, pero ya hemos visto que los imposibles no existen y que no se puede descartar nada. Dicho esto, Cook se encuentra extremadamente cómodo en su nuevo rol como presidente ejecutivo de Apple. Además, no es un directivo enfocado en producto como sí lo fue Jensen Huang ; algo que podría no importar en cualquier otra empresa, pero que ha sido crucial para el crecimiento de NVIDIA bajo el comando de un único CEO en sus 33 años de vida. Ya veremos qué novedades surgen en tal sentido.

sources.name: El Confidencial Tecnologia
sources.title: ¿Quién podrá suceder a Jensen Huang como nuevo CEO de Nvidia? Los candidatos, sus trayectorias y a qué se dedican
sources.text: Nvidia se enfrenta a uno de los momentos más delicados de su historia. La compañía estadounidense, convertida en una pieza fundamental del desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial, se ha quedado sin el único consejero delegado que ha conocido desde su fundación en 1993. Las informaciones sobre las presuntas relaciones extramatrimoniales de Jensen Huang, una de ellas con una supuesta agente vinculada a China, han provocado una crisis que ha terminado con su salida. Según ha publicado The Wall Street Journal, la empresa estaba preparando su destitución, pero ha sido el consejo de administración quien, tras convocar una reunión extraordinaria para estudiar su futuro, ha terminado por dimitir. La situación ha adquirido una dimensión todavía mayor después de que The New York Times informase de una segunda relación extramatrimonial, esta vez con una ejecutiva de la propia compañía. Ahora que Huang ha tomado la decisión de salir, antes de que Nvidia confirmara oficialmente la destitución de Huang, la pregunta es clara: ¿quién dirigirá Nvidia sin Jensen Huang? Uno de los nombres que más fuerza ha cobrado es el de Colette Kress, vicepresidenta ejecutiva y directora financiera de Nvidia. Según recoge el Financial Times, fuentes próximas a la compañía consideran que sería la alternativa más sencilla para garantizar una transición ordenada si Huang abandona el cargo. Por el momento, es ella, precisamente, quien ha tomado el relevo de forma temporal. Kress llegó a Nvidia en septiembre de 2013 después de acumular una amplia experiencia en algunas de las principales empresas tecnológicas de Estados Unidos. Anteriormente, trabajó durante tres años en Cisco, donde fue responsable de la estrategia financiera, la planificación y el desarrollo de negocio de diferentes divisiones. También pasó 13 años en Microsoft, cuatro de ellos como directora financiera de su división de servidores y herramientas, y ocupó distintos puestos en Texas Instruments. Licenciada en Finanzas por la Universidad de Arizona y con un MBA por la Universidad Metodista del Sur, Kress conoce de primera mano las operaciones económicas de Nvidia y mantiene una relación estrecha con los inversores. Su experiencia gestionando las finanzas de grandes multinacionales tecnológicas podría resultar fundamental para tranquilizar a los mercados durante una posible transición. Sin embargo, su principal debilidad frente a otros candidatos es que no cuenta con una formación técnica comparable a la de Huang. Aunque domina las cuentas y la estrategia financiera, dirigir Nvidia también exige comprender una industria marcada por la innovación constante y la competencia por desarrollar los chips más avanzados. Si el consejo de administración apuesta por un perfil tecnológico, Ian Buck podría convertirse en uno de los principales aspirantes. El ingeniero se incorporó a Nvidia en 2004, después de completar su doctorado en Informática en la Universidad de Stanford, y actualmente ocupa el cargo de vicepresidente de computación a hiperescala y de alto rendimiento. Su trayectoria está estrechamente vinculada a uno de los mayores éxitos de Nvidia: CUDA, la plataforma que permite utilizar las tarjetas gráficas para realizar cálculos complejos y que hoy utilizan millones de desarrolladores, investigadores y científicos. Buck fue uno de sus principales impulsores y contribuyó a transformar las GPU en herramientas fundamentales para la inteligencia artificial. Actualmente, supervisa productos de hardware y software destinados a grandes clientes tecnológicos como Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta y OpenAI. Su trabajo consiste en colaborar con estas compañías para desarrollar e implementar soluciones de inteligencia artificial generativa, una de las áreas más importantes del negocio de Nvidia. Además, Buck cuenta con experiencia institucional. Ha comparecido ante el Congreso de Estados Unidos para abordar cuestiones relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial, ha asesorado a la Casa Blanca y ha participado en proyectos internacionales para desarrollar superordenadores destinados a la investigación científica. Su principal fortaleza es el profundo conocimiento técnico de los productos de Nvidia. Sin embargo, a diferencia de Kress, no pertenece al círculo más cercano de Huang, lo que podría dificultar su elección como sustituto inmediato. Entre las alternativas externas destaca Lisa Su, presidenta y consejera delegada de AMD, uno de los principales competidores de Nvidia. Su nombre resulta especialmente atractivo por su experiencia liderando la transformación de una empresa tecnológica y reforzando su posición en el mercado de los semiconductores. Su llegó a AMD en enero de 2012 como vicepresidenta sénior y directora general de sus unidades de negocio. Posteriormente, asumió la dirección de operaciones, desde donde impulsó la integración de diferentes departamentos y contribuyó a reorganizar la compañía. Su trayectoria anterior incluye puestos de responsabilidad en Freescale Semiconductor, IBM y Texas Instruments. A diferencia de otros posibles candidatos, Su combina una sólida formación técnica con experiencia empresarial y capacidad de gestión. Durante sus 13 años en IBM desempeñó diferentes funciones de ingeniería y dirección, incluida la vicepresidencia de su centro de investigación y desarrollo de semiconductores. Su liderazgo también ha recibido numerosos reconocimientos. En 2024 fue elegida consejera delegada del año por la revista TIME y en 2026 recibió la Medalla Nacional de Ciencias de Estados Unidos, uno de los principales reconocimientos científicos del país. Su posible incorporación a Nvidia, sin embargo, presenta un obstáculo evidente. Y es que actualmente dirige una de las compañías que compiten directamente con ella. Convencerla para abandonar AMD supondría una operación extraordinaria, aunque su experiencia gestionando grandes transformaciones empresariales la convierte en una de las figuras más preparadas para afrontar un relevo de estas características.

sources.name: El Confidencial Tecnologia
sources.title: Dimite Jensen Huang, CEO de Nvidia, tras el escándalo de sus infidelidades y su relación con una espía china
sources.text: El hombre más importante para la industria de la IA en estos momentos se marcha. Jensen Huang, CEO de Nvidia, ha presentado su renuncia. Una decisión que llega tras cuatro días en el ojo del huracán después de que la compañía anunciase que iba a investigar la relación extramatrimonial que mantuvo con una empresaria china cliente de la multinacional que, en realidad, sería una presunta agente de inteligencia de Pekín. Este final parece haberse precipitado horas después de que trascendiera un segundo affaire, en esta ocasión con una subordinada directa. La junta directiva mantuvo este miércoles un encuentro en el que se puso su despido sobre la mesa. Finalmente, no han tenido que obligar a Huang a marcharse, sino que ha decidido dimitir, tal y como ha adelantado la agencia Reuters. La polémica ha afectado y mucho al valor de la compañía, que hasta hace apenas diez días presumía de ser la empresa con mayor capitalización bursátil del mundo, puesto que recuperó Apple el pasado 3 de noviembre. En las últimas cinco sesiones, Nvidia ha perdido cerca de 470.000 millones de dólares. Algo que ha profundizado en una caída que se inició hace un mes, cuando ha visto esfumarse 1,33 billones de su valor. En cuatro semanas ha pasado de 5,52 billones de dólares de valor en Bolsa a 4,19 billones tras el cierre de los mercados este miércoles. Nada más abrir los mercados, sus títulos caían más de un 14%. Y es previsible que esa caída pueda acentuarse en los próximos días, porque su sucesión no es precisamente sencilla. De momento, Colette Kress , directora financiera, será la que asumirá de forma interina el rol de CEO. La junta ha asegurado que se pone en marcha para buscar un candidato para reemplazarle de forma definitiva, sondeando opciones tanto fuera como dentro de la compañía. Hasta que saltó el escándalo de la presunta trampa de miel tendida por una espía china (un extremo, por cierto, que Pekín niega), nadie había cuestionado públicamente el liderazgo hiperpersonalista que Jensen Huang ejecutaba sobre la organización. Durante más de 30 años, el tiempo que ha pasado desde que fundó la compañía en 1993, ha creado y mantenido una estructura en la que prácticamente todas las decisiones de negocio, fuesen del ámbito que fuesen, eran supervisadas por él. Él dirigía y controlaba a un grupo de sesenta ejecutivos que le reportaban diariamente. A diferencia de otras grandes tecnológicas, concentró todo el negocio en su figura. No hubo nunca un presidente ni un vicepresidente ejecutivo que estuviese llamado a reemplazarle. Esto no era sinónimo de que hubiese un plan a largo plazo. El propio Huang había colocado a sus hijos y su yerno en puestos de alta responsabilidad como si se tratase de una empresa familiar. Es cierto que el fundador era el máximo accionista (con un 4% de los títulos) pero estos nombramientos llamaron la atención en su momento porque ninguno de ellos tenía experiencia previa en el sector tecnológico. Su hija Madison se formó en pastelería y trabajó en el grupo LVMH. Spencer, por su parte, regentaba un bar en Taiwán. Sin embargo, su padre les empujó a estudiar en el MIT, así como cursar estudios superiores de administración de empresas. Su falta de experiencia en otras grandes tecnológicas no fue obstáculo para que se les adjudicasen sueldos millonarios y se les pusiera al frente de divisiónes como la de realidad virtual o robótica. Sin embargo, la tormenta en torno a las relaciones extramatrimoniales de su padre y el presunto espionaje de Pekín ha desbarato sus opciones para una sucesión familiar. Una decisión que llega tras cuatro días en el ojo del huracán después de que la compañía anunciase que iba a investigar la relación extramatrimonial que mantuvo con una empresaria china cliente de la multinacional que, en realidad, sería una presunta agente de inteligencia de Pekín. Este final parece haberse precipitado horas después de que trascendiera un segundo affaire, en esta ocasión con una subordinada directa. sources.title: NVIDIA podría destituir a Jensen Huang como CEO tras el escándalo con la espía china
sources.text: Jensen Huang podría perder su puesto como director ejecutivo de NVIDIA . De acuerdo con The Wall Street Journal , la junta directiva estaría preparando una reunión para decidir el futuro del fundador y CEO de la compañía. Las cosas se complicaron para Huang luego de que una investigación interna descubriera vínculos con una supuesta espía china. Según el reporte, el consejo de administración considera destituir a Huang después de que salieran a la luz dos relaciones extramaritales . Hace unos días, el CEO reconoció que había sido infiel a su esposa y pidió disculpas por traicionar la confianza de su familia y de la organización. La figura en el centro de esa polémica es Alice Huang, una ejecutiva de la compañía Megaspeed y con vínculos con el gobierno de Xi Jinping. Los primeros rumores apuntaban a que Megaspeed habría ayudado a desviar chips de IA hacia China . La compañía, con sede en Singapur, se convirtió en uno de los principales clientes de NVIDIA para la construcción de centros de datos de IA en el sudeste asiático. No obstante, las autoridades estadounidenses sospecharon que Huang ayudó a contrabandear tarjetas gráficas , por lo cual abrieron una investigación a finales de 2024. La relación entre Jensen Huang y Alice Huang comenzó en 2023 y permitió que la ejecutiva china desviara 240.000 placas gráficas H100, H200 y A100 hacia el gigante asiático. The Information reveló que Huang montó una red de empresas en China junto con su hermana y esposo, incluyendo una que le ayudó a convertirse en socio preferente de NVIDIA. Este movimiento le garantizó acceso prioritario a los chips y al CEO de la empresa. Hace unas semanas surgió un reporte de que Alice Huang estaba vinculada a los servicios de inteligencia chinos. El Departamento de Justicia abrió múltiples investigaciones relacionadas con ella y el mundo se le vino encima al jefe de NVIDIA. Según informó el New York Times , Alice Huang (también conocida como Huang Le) trabajaba para el Ministerio de Seguridad del Estado de China mientras mantenía una relación romántica con el directivo de la empresa de tarjetas gráficas. Los investigadores temen que pueda haber accedido a detalles técnicos sobre el hardware de IA de NVIDIA y las discusiones internas con la Casa Blanca. Hasta ahora, las autoridades se han centrado en su papel como ejecutiva de Megaspeed, donde aprovechó su cercanía con Jensen Huang para ayudar a eludir los controles de exportación estadounidenses. Además de esta relación, el New York Times señaló que el jefe de NVIDIA mantuvo un romance con otra empleada de la compañía . Kimberly Powell, vicepresidente del área de atención médica de NVIDIA, fue captada en un vídeo con Jensen Huang mientras se encontraban en un hotel de San José, California. Las políticas internas de la compañía prohíben este tipo de acciones, sobre todo cuando se trata de una relación extramarital entre un jefe y su subordinada. Hasta el momento de esta publicación, el futuro de Jensen Huang permanece en el aire . Si la junta decide apartarlo del cargo, NVIDIA perdería al hombre que transformó la compañía y la convirtió en una de las más valiosas del mundo. Huang ha sido el rostro visible de la empresa por más de tres décadas, primero en su etapa gamer y ahora en el desarrollo de chips para centros de datos, por lo que encontrar un sucesor será un trabajo complejo.

sources.title: Jensen Huang dimite como CEO de NVIDIA tras el escándalo que sacude a la compañía: Colette Kress toma el mando
sources.text: Elígenos como tu fuente preferida en Google. Jensen Huang, hasta ahora máximo responsable de NVIDIA, ha presentado su dimisión después de conocerse el escándalo de espionaje internacional que sacude a la compañía. Colette Kress, hasta ahora directora financiera, ha sido nombrada CEO interina mientras se busca un sustituto definitivo. Jensen Huang ha presentado su dimisión como CEO NVIDIA, con efecto inmediato . La compañía ha nombrado a Colette Kress, hasta ahora directora financiera, CEO interina mientras se busca a un sustituto definitivo. La salida del que ha sido el rostro más visible de la compañía llega en plena crisis reputacional por las informaciones sobre su vida personal y un posible caso de espionaje internacional. La dimisión de Huang supone un cambio histórico para NVIDIA, empresa que cofundó en 1993 y que ha dirigido durante más de tres décadas. Bajo su liderazgo, la multinacional ha pasado de ser uno de los principales fabricantes de tarjetas gráficas para videojuegos a convertirse en una pieza fundamental de la industria tecnológica gracias a sus procesadores para IA . Esta decisión llega después de varias informaciones sobre supuestas relaciones extramatrimoniales de Huang, una de ellas con Alice Huang, una empresaria china sobre la que las autoridades estadounidenses habrían mostrado sospechas por sus posibles vínculos con los servicios de inteligencia de Pekín . También han trascendido varios rumores sobre una posible segunda relación con Kimberly Powell, una directiva de NVIDIA que trabajaba bajo su supervisión. Todo esto habría llevado al consejo de administración de la empresa a abrir una investigación independiente para determinar si Huang había sido objetivo de una operación de inteligencia china para filtrar y robar información. La persona que asumirá provisionalmente las riendas de NVIDIA será Colette Kress , que lleva en la compañía desde septiembre de 2013 y hasta ahora ocupaba el puesto de vicepresidenta ejecutiva y directora financiera. Kress mantendrá también sus responsabilidades económicas mientras el consejo de administración busca un sustituto permanente. Antes de incorporarse a NVIDIA, la directiva acumuló cerca de 25 años de experiencia en departamentos financieros de grandes tecnológicas , entre ellas Cisco y Microsoft. El consejo considera que su experiencia de las cuentas, así como del funcionamiento interno de la compañía la convierten en una figura relevante para garantizar la continuidad del negocio durante esta transición. La compañía también ha anunciado el nombramiento de Harvey C. Jones como presidente del consejo de administración . Se trata de un movimiento significativo, ya que será el primer presidente de la junta directiva en la historia de NVIDIA. Jones lleva formando parte del consejo desde 1993 y cuenta con una larga trayectoria en el sector tecnológico y de la inversión. La dimisión de Jensen Huang llega en un momento especialmente delicado para el fabricante de chips . Su figura ha sido fundamental para construir la identidad de la compañía y establecer relaciones estratégicas con los principales proveedores de servicios en la nube, desarrolladores de inteligencia artificial y fabricantes de hardware. Además, el directivo había defendido públicamente la necesidad de mantener el acceso de NVIDIA al mercado chino , incluso en un contexto de restricciones estadounidenses a la exportación de semiconductores avanzados. Su salida también introduce incertidumbre sobre la posición que adoptará la compañía en este terreno. El consejo de administración de la compañía ha transmitido un mensaje de continuidad y confianza en el equipo directivo. La empresa asegura que sus operaciones y sus compromisos con los clientes no se verán afectados.

sources.title: Nvidia busca CEO tras la salida de Jensen Huang: estos son los candidatos que suenan para el puesto
sources.text: Nvidia ha perdido al único director ejecutivo que ha tenido jamás. Jensen Huang ha dimitido este jueves como presidente, director ejecutivo y miembro del consejo de administración, y la empresa ahora tiene que encontrar a alguien para dirigir al fabricante de chips más valioso del mundo. Por el momento, el puesto pertenece a alguien de la casa. Qué ha pasado. Nvidia anunciaba que su directora financiera, Colette Kress, actuará como directora ejecutiva interina mientras mantiene su cargo financiero, y que el consejo buscará candidatos internos y externos para el puesto permanente. También ha nombrado a Harvey C. Jones, antiguo director ejecutivo de Synopsys, como presidente del consejo, siendo de hecho el primero en la historia de la empresa. La salida de Huang se produce tras las investigaciones sobre sus relaciones extramatrimoniales, una de ellas presuntamente con Alice Huang , ejecutiva y directora de la empresa Megaspeed, sospechosa de ser espía china . Las acciones de Nvidia abrieron este jueves con una caída de más del 13 % tras la dimisión, borrando más de medio billón de dólares en valor. La nueva CEO interina : Colette Kress. Ha sido directora financiera desde 2013, trabajó anteriormente en Cisco y Microsoft, y aparece junto a Huang en cada presentación de resultados. Josh Gilbert, analista de eToro, declaraba a Reuters que es “la opción obvia para mantener el rumbo” y una voz de confianza para los inversores. Ahora, que se quede de forma permanente es otra cosa. Para Gilbert la ventaja de Nvidia es la tecnología y el consejo probablemente querría a un ingeniero al mando. Los ingenieros. Ian Buck, quien ayudó a desarrollar CUDA, el software que mantiene a los desarrolladores vinculados a los chips de Nvidia, y que ahora dirige los productos de IA a hiperescala, encabeza la lista para llevarse el puesto permanente. Shay Boloor, estratega jefe de mercado en Futurum Equities, contaba a Reuters que es el candidato interno más fuerte por ese motivo. Otros miembros internos mencionados incluyen al cofundador Chris Malachowsky, el único ejecutivo al nivel de antigüedad de Huang, y a Andrew Bell, vicepresidente sénior de ingeniería de hardware, con una trayectoria destacada en el sector de los chips. Los externos. Si el consejo mira más allá de Nvidia, que es algo que también plantean según el comunicado, el nombre que más suena es el del director ejecutivo de Arm, Rene Haas, antiguo ejecutivo de Nvidia. Tiene “sentido lógico”, según comparten en Reuters, pero tal y como comparte Charu Chanana, estratega de inversiones del banco Saxo, el modelo de negocio de Arm difiere considerablemente del de Nvidia. ¿Y la familia? . Los dos hijos de Huang ocupan cargos ejecutivos en Nvidia, aunque todavía son relativamente jóvenes e “inexpertos”, según relatan desde la BBC. Armina Rosenberg, de Minotaur Capital, ve plausible también una estructura de codirección ejecutiva, combinando a un líder financiero como Kress con un líder tecnológico como Buck. Qué pasa ahora. De momento, y hasta conocer más noticias, tendremos que esperar al próximo martes 17 de noviembre, que es cuando Nvidia presenta sus resultados del tercer trimestre bajo el mando de Kress.
